newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 21.

text.p: - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- CBI SLASHES FORECAST FOR GROWTH

The Confederation of British Industry has cut its forecasts of economic and profits growth due to fears about the strength of sterling and export prospects. The revised figure for economic growth this year is 2.8 per cent, which is a reduction of 0.3 points on predictions made three months ago. Predictions of growth in manufacturing output, capital investment and exports have also been lowered after CBI economists decided their earlier predictions were over optimistic.
-- IMI TO CUT LOSSES WITH CLOSURE OF YORKSHIRE COPPER PLANT

The engineering group, IMI is to close its copper alloys business in Yorkshire at the cost of 670 jobs. The group announced yesterday that it had failed to find a buyer for its loss making business and the operation would shut down at a cost of 25 million pounds stg. The business had lost over 19 million pounds over the last five years, and according to a director of the company, had no prospect of it returning to profits.
-- BASS SELECTS AMERICAN TO MANAGE HOLIDAY INN

Bass yesterday recruited Tom Oliver, a 56-year old American, to head its internationAL hotels business, Holiday Inn. The appointment fills the vacancy left when former chief executive, Tim Lane resigned after just six months in the post. One priority will be to expand Crowne Plaza, the 127-strong chain of four-star hotels.
THE TIMES
-- BARINGS BONDHOLDERS COULD BE IN LINE FOR SETTLEMENT

ING Barings are looking for a suitable mechanism to make compensation payouts to the thousands of Barings bondholders who lost 275 million pounds stg in the collapse of the merchant bank nearly two years ago. Any deal would have to be cleared by the UK courts as being "fair and reasonable".
-- RANK GROUP EXPANSION TO CREATE 3,000 JOBS IN LEISURE

The Rank Group's continued expansion will create 3,000 jobs in its diverse leisure interests. The largest of its new developments includes a 25 million pounds stg entertainment complex in Southampton as well as a 100 million pounds stg Oasis Forest Holiday Village in Penrith, Cumbria. The group also plans to expand it's Hard Rock brand as well as develop 20 new Tom Cobleigh pubs.
-- BBC IN FLEXTECH PAY TV LINK

The BBC approved in principle a joint venture with Flextech, the cable and satellite TV programmer yesterday, to launch the BBC's first subscription channels later this year. The 150 million pounds stg venture was agreed with qualifications at the BBC board of governors' meeting with an official announcement expected by the end of the month.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SCOTTISH PRIDE CALLS IN RECEIVERS

Scottish Pride, the Glasgow based dairy group have called in the receivers following the group's loss of a crucial contract with Safeway supermarkets. Redundancies have been vowed to be kept to a minimum by the receiver, hoping to find a buyer soon, but it is thought that the jobs of 763 people are at risk. The group made losses last year of 4.17 million pounds stg on a turnover of 96 million pounds stg. -- POWER CHIEF CALLS FOR INQUIRY INTO POOL PRICES

Government plans to cut electricity prices by introducing competition to the domestic market will fail if there is not a drastic reform of the Pool, the wholesale power market at the centre of the privatised industry according to Malcolm Chatwin, chief executive of Yorkshire Electricity. Mr Chatwin claims that there is growing support among regional electricity companies for a Monopolies Commission inquiry into the Pool and the margins being made by power generation companies.
-- UKRAINE 'NEEDS AID' TO FINISH REACTORS

Ukraine will continue to call for western aid in a bid to complete the two nuclear reactors which would offset power lost form closure of the remaining reactors at Chenobyl. An independent panel, commissioned by the EBRD, this week decided the completion of the two reactors did not meet its key lending test. The EBRD will seek clarification of the panel's assumptions and reasoning.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- RAILTRACK PROMISES TO INVEST OVER 4 MILLION POUNDS A DAY

Railtrack will spend more than 4 million pounds stg a day on the rail network over the next 10 years. Railtrack, the company that owns the UK's track, signalling and stations. A total of 16 billion pounds stg will be invested including spending over 1 billion pounds stg on stations, 2.5 billion pounds stg on track work and more than 2 billion pounds stg on signalling. The company will have to borrow 2.5 billion pounds stg finance spending.
-- WELSH WATER'S PRICING UNDER INVESTIGATION

Ofwat, the water regulator, is investigating claims that Welsh Water is engaged in predatory pricing tactics to stifle a move to introduce competition into the privatised industry. The dispute involves Shotton Paper's move to switch from Welsh Water to a new supplier. Enviro-Logic, a London based consultancy, claim it can slash Shotton's, who are one of the UK's largest paper producers, 2 million pounds water bill by exploiting a provision in the Water Act known as an inset appointment. Welsh Water is thought to have responded by offering to cut its own charges to Shotton, although Enviro-Logic believe they promised to undercut any price put forward by the consultancy group, thus abusing it's monopoly powers.
-- SCOTAM GIVES UP FLOAT PLANS AND ASKS FOR BIDS

Scottish Amicable gave up it's flotation plans yesterday and offered potential bidders a week to table their bids. Up to six companies may be in the running for what is the first public auction for a mutual life insurer. Two of the bidders have already shown, they are Abbey National and Prudential, with Australian Mutual Provident widely tipped to be in the frame.
